comments.author: Alexander Terp
comments.body:
**Units: decided, and it is not what the description says.** Support
both, spelled with a required suffix - `resize_step = "150px"` and
`resize_step = "20c"`.

The description above argues for cells alone. The argument that beat it
is the asymmetry: a cell is about 8x17 points, so one number in cells
moves a divider roughly 160pt sideways and 340pt vertically. Four
symmetric chords that move visibly different distances is not what a hand
expects, and pixels are the unit a "nudge the divider" gesture is
actually felt in. Cells keep their own advantage - they survive a font
size change, which pixels do not, and ⌘+ is a thing people press - so
neither is right for everybody.

**The suffix is required rather than optional**, and that is the whole of
what makes two units safe. A bare `20` meaning cells beside a suffixed
`"150px"` is a form you have to know rather than read; with both
suffixed there is nothing to guess. It also means the currently shipping
bare `resize_step = 2` stops parsing, which is a breaking change to say
plainly in a release note - and cheap now, in a way it will not be later.

`c` rather than `ce` or `cells`: kitty already spells this exact
ambiguity that way (`initial_window_width 80c`, bare or `px` for pixels),
so anyone arriving from a terminal that solved it has one less thing to
learn.

Cost is close to nothing once pixels exist at all. The shell has to
measure cell size and convert regardless, because the daemon's resize is
grid-based - so cells is the identity case of a conversion that has to be
written anyway.

Consistency question to answer in the same pass rather than leave ragged:
`pane_padding` is points and bare. The rule that seems right is to suffix
only where two units are genuinely plausible - nobody wants padding in
cells - but that asymmetry should read as a decision in the docs rather
than as an oversight.

comments.author: Alexander Terp
comments.body:
**Decided: `[keymap]` stays keyed by action, and the mechanism does not
get built.** Neither shape in the description wins - the question turns
out to be settled by a constraint neither of them mentions.

**On macOS the keymap is the menu.** Every action is a menu item, a menu
item has exactly one key equivalent, and that is also how System Settings
finds a shortcut to override. Ghostty's chord-keyed form lets you write
two chords for one action, or a binding with no action name at all -
configs the menu cannot represent and the platform cannot rebind. That
rules out keying by chord on a Muster-specific ground rather than on
taste, and it is the kind of reason worth having written down, because
the next person to arrive from Ghostty will ask again.

That leaves the inline-table shape, and it has nothing to carry.
`resize_step` and `scroll_multiplier` are root keys already, they cover
what prompted this, and no second parameterized action is waiting.

**So `focus_tab_1` through `focus_tab_9` staying nine names is correct
rather than a wart to unpick.** Nine menu items need nine actions. The
core carrying `Action::FocusTab(u8)` internally is the right shape: the
config file names menu items, the core names intents. (Note that when
a_294D7XaZl lands these become nine pane actions, and the same reasoning
carries over unchanged.)

**One rule to write into architecture.md while settling this**, because
it is what keeps this decision from constraining the CLI: **the intent is
parameterized, the action is not.** `CreateTab { workspace, cwd }` already
takes arguments; `new_tab` is a parameterless name that dispatches it with
defaults. The CLI (a_26BJb2n6o) names intents directly and passes
arguments, so it does not inherit the menu's one-chord-per-item
constraint. Two surfaces onto one path, which is what the parity
desideratum promised.

**What is left of this card is the units work** from the comment above -
both units, required suffix, `"150px"` and `"20c"` - plus documenting
that a Ghostty `resize_split:left,150` becomes `resize_step` here and
moves a different distance unless you suffix it. The bare
`resize_step = 2` shipping today stops parsing, and that belongs in a
release note.

creator: Alexander Terp
description:
Ghostty spells resize as `cmd+shift+h=resize_split:left,150` - the chord
names the action *and* how far it goes. Muster's `[keymap]` is keyed by
action and every action is parameterless, so there is nowhere to put the
150.

**Most of what prompted this already works**, and is worth saying before
anyone builds: `resize_step` is a root key in `~/.muster/config.toml`
(whole cells, omit for the daemon's own step), and `scroll_multiplier` is
too. A config wanting all four directions to move the same amount - which
is what the Ghostty snippet above actually does - is one line today.

So the gap is narrower than it looks, and it is a design question rather
than a missing feature: **should a chord be able to carry an argument?**

Muster already has exactly one parameterized action and dodged the
question - `focus_tab_1` through `focus_tab_9` are nine action names for
one action, and the core carries the number as `Action::FocusTab(u8)`
internally while the config file sees nine strings. That worked because
nine is small and the numbers are a closed set. Resize amounts are not
closed, so this is where the question gets asked properly.

Two shapes, and they are not equivalent:

- **Keep the keymap keyed by action, and let a value ride along** -
  `resize_left = { chord = "cmd+shift+h", cells = 20 }`, or a second
  table. Stays inside the existing rule that an action has one chord, and
  makes the argument obviously a setting rather than part of the chord.
- **Key by chord with arguments, as Ghostty does.** More familiar to
  anyone arriving from Ghostty, and it breaks the current rule -
  `[keymap]` is keyed by action precisely because an action has one chord
  and `[text]` is keyed by chord precisely because text has no name to
  key on. A third scheme needs to justify itself against that split.

Worth deciding rather than defaulting, and there is an ordering argument
for deciding it now rather than when the second parameterized action
arrives: whatever this picks, `focus_tab_N` should stop being nine names
for one action, and the cost of unpicking that grows with every config
file somebody writes.

Units are the other half. `resize_step` is **cells**; Ghostty's number is
pixels. Cells are the more meaningful unit for a grid of terminals - "two
more rows" survives a font size change and "150 pixels" does not - and it
means a config carried over from Ghostty will move a different distance
than it did there. That is the right answer and a surprise worth naming
in the docs rather than leaving somebody to discover.
title: ⌨️ A keybinding that carries an argument, starting with resize amounts
